scenarios.title: Verify a partner by MPN id
gotchas: Omit mpnId to return the signed-in partner's profile.

scenarios.title: Get a list of customers
gotchas: Paged collection: response has totalCount, items[], and links (follow links.next for more pages).
Each item carries only companyProfile and relationshipToPartner; call get-customer-by-id for full detail.
Filter with &filter={url-encoded-json} to search by company name, domain, or reseller.

scenarios.title: Create a customer

headers.name: MS-RequestId
headers.note: GUID for idempotency; reuse the same value on retries so the customer isn't created twice

requestFields.name: CompanyProfile.domain
requestFields.note: e.g. contoso.onmicrosoft.com

requestFields.name: BillingProfile.culture
requestFields.note: e.g. en-US

requestFields.name: BillingProfile.language
requestFields.note: two-letter code, e.g. en

requestFields.name: BillingProfile.defaultAddress
requestFields.note: validate via validate-address first

requestFields.name: CompanyProfile.organizationRegistrationNumber
requestFields.note: required in some countries (RU, TR, BR, IN, UAE, ...)

requestFields.name: enableGDAPByDefault
requestFields.note: only honored in clouds that support GDAP

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch("https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers", { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json", "MS-RequestId": crypto.randomUUID(), "MS-CorrelationId": crypto.randomUUID() }, body });

gotchas: Returns 201 with a Customer that includes userCredentials (admin username/password) - save it, it cannot be retrieved later.
Idempotent: reuse the same MS-RequestId on retries to avoid creating duplicate customers.
Required body: BillingProfile (email, culture, language, companyName, defaultAddress) and CompanyProfile (domain).
A valid physical address is required; in the sandbox an invalid address makes the customer tenant undeletable.
organizationRegistrationNumber is mandatory for customers in certain countries/regions (e.g. Russia, Turkey, Brazil, India, UAE).
Do not pass a userCredentials password in the request; it is not accepted.
Also supports app-only.

scenarios.title: Get a customer by ID
gotchas: customer-id is the customer's Microsoft (Entra) tenant GUID.
Without DAP/GDAP access the response omits CompanyProfileAddress, CompanyProfileEmail, and CustomDomain.
Supports both app+user and app-only.

scenarios.title: Delete a customer from the integration sandbox

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}`, { method: "DELETE", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });

gotchas: Sandbox (TIP) only - this breaks the partner-customer relationship and purges ALL resources for that tenant.
Returns 204 No Content on success.
All Azure reservations and software purchase orders must be canceled first or the delete fails.
A customer created with an invalid sandbox address cannot be deleted.

scenarios.title: Create a user account for a customer

requestFields.name: userPrincipalName
requestFields.note: must use the customer's own (non-federated) domain

requestFields.name: usageLocation
requestFields.note: two-letter country code

requestFields.name: passwordProfile.password
requestFields.note: auto-generated if omitted; must meet complexity rules

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/users`, { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body });

gotchas: App+User only - app-only is NOT supported. Requires a GDAP role (User Administrator or Directory Writers).
Returns 200 OK (not 201) with the created CustomerUser including its generated id.
userPrincipalName must use the customer's own (non-federated) domain.
passwordProfile.password must meet complexity rules; set forceChangePassword=true to require a reset on first sign-in.

scenarios.title: Get all user accounts for a customer
gotchas: App+User only - app-only is NOT supported. Requires a GDAP role (Directory Reader, Global Reader, or User Administrator).
For a single user, use /v1/customers/{customer-id}/users/{user-id}.

scenarios.title: Assign licenses to a user

requestFields.name: licensesToAssign
requestFields.note: each item has skuId and optional excludedPlans

requestFields.name: licensesToRemove
requestFields.note: skuIds to unassign

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/users/${userId}/licenseupdates`, { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body });

gotchas: Returns 201 with the LicenseUpdate resource on success.
Fails if the license is not available in the customer tenant; get valid skuId values from get-subscribed-skus first.
licensesToAssign and licensesToRemove must reference SKUs from the same license group; verify the result with get-user-licenses.

scenarios.title: Get a list of products

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch("https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/products?country=US&targetView=OnlineServices", { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, Accept: "application/json" } });

gotchas: Both country and targetView are required.
targetView is an enum (Azure, AzureReservations, MicrosoftAzure, OnlineServices, Software, MarketplaceSaaS); use OnlineServices for new commerce (NCE) license-based products.
For Azure Reservations add reservationScope=AzurePlan.
403/400036 if the targetView is not allowed; 403/400030 if the targetSegment is not allowed.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

scenarios.title: Get a list of availabilities for a SKU

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/products/${productId}/skus/${skuId}/availabilities?country=US`, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, Accept: "application/json" } });

gotchas: country is required; all segments except nonprofit are returned by default (pass targetSegment=nonprofit explicitly for those).
The availability's CatalogItemId is mutable and reissued regularly - always fetch a fresh availability right before adding a cart line item or placing an order.
For Azure Reservation SKUs add reservationScope=AzurePlan; add IncludeLifeCycleState=true for NCE license-based lifecycle state.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

scenarios.title: Create a cart

requestFields.name: lineItems
requestFields.note: >=1 item; processed in array order

requestFields.name: lineItems[].id
requestFields.note: zero-based line index

requestFields.name: lineItems[].catalogItemId
requestFields.note: fresh value from get-sku-availabilities

requestFields.name: lineItems[].termDuration
requestFields.note: ISO 8601 (P1M, P1Y); omit for Azure plan & perpetual software

requestFields.name: lineItems[].billingCycle
requestFields.note: snake_case: monthly, annual, one_time

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/carts`, { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body });

gotchas: Carts expire 7 days after creation. Success returns 201 with the populated Cart.
lineItems is required (>=1 CartLineItem). Line items are processed in array order - place any promotion-eligible (New-To-Offer) item FIRST.
billingCycle uses snake_case JSON enum values (one_time, monthly, none).
Azure plan and perpetual software line items do NOT support termDuration - omit it for those.
Set AttestationAccepted per line item when the offer enforces attestation.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

scenarios.title: Check out a cart

examples.csharp: var res = await http.PostAsync($"/v1/customers/{customerId}/carts/{cartId}/checkout", new StringContent("", Encoding.UTF8, "application/json")); // 201 Created
examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/carts/${cartId}/checkout`, { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" } });

gotchas: Empty request body (Content-Length: 0). Success returns 201 with a CartCheckoutResult containing an orders array.
Idempotent: re-checking out an already-checked-out cart returns the original result.
Provisioning is asynchronous - subscriptionId values may be absent in the response and appear later via Get Order.
Checkout fails on an expired cart (7-day limit).
Supports both app-only and app+user.

scenarios.title: Get an order by ID
gotchas: Use this (or list-customer-orders) to retrieve subscriptionId values not yet provisioned at checkout time.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

scenarios.title: Get all of a customer's orders
gotchas: There is a delay of up to 15 minutes between order submission and appearance in this collection - don't poll immediately after checkout.
Optional ?billingType={monthly|annual|one_time|none} filters by billing cycle.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

scenarios.title: List a customer's subscriptions
gotchas: Supports both app-only and app+user.
customer-tenant-id is the customer's Microsoft (Entra) tenant GUID.

scenarios.title: Get a subscription by ID
gotchas: Add-on subscriptions include parentSubscriptionId.
NCE subscriptions return extra fields (productType, termDuration, billingCycle, refundOptions, cancellationAllowedUntilDate).
Supports both app-only and app+user.

scenarios.title: Update a subscription (quantity, status, autorenew)

requestFields.name: (full Subscription resource)
requestFields.note: GET the subscription, mutate, then PATCH the whole object back

requestFields.name: quantity
requestFields.note: seat count

requestFields.name: status
requestFields.note: active | suspended (suspend/reactivate)

requestFields.name: autoRenewEnabled
requestFields.note: include it or it silently resets to false

examples.csharp:
var req = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Patch, $"/v1/customers/{customerId}/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}") { Content = content };
var res = await http.SendAsync(req);
examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/subscriptions/${subscriptionId}`, { method: "PATCH", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body });

gotchas: Send the FULL Subscription resource, not a partial patch: GET it first, mutate it, then PATCH it back.
If autoRenewEnabled or next-term instructions are set, include them in the body or they are silently reset.
Change quantity via Quantity; suspend/reactivate via Status (active/suspended); toggle renewal via AutoRenewEnabled.
Cancel an NCE subscription within its cancellation window by PATCHing Status to 'deleted' (see cancellationAllowedUntilDate).
Schedule changes for the next term (term/quantity/billing at renewal) via scheduledNextTermInstructions.
NCE license quantity can only be reduced within 7 days of purchase/renewal (else error 800090).
Billing cycle CANNOT be changed here (error 2054) - use update-order instead.
For SKU/term upgrades or trial-to-paid, use create-subscription-transition instead.
Long-running updates return 202 with a Location header to poll.

scenarios.title: Get a list of subscriptions by order
gotchas: Note the underscore: order_id, not orderId.
Returns a collection even when the order produced a single subscription.
Up to 15-minute delay after order submission before subscriptions appear.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

scenarios.title: Migrate a legacy subscription to New Commerce (NCE)

requestFields.name: currentSubscriptionId
requestFields.note: the legacy subscription to migrate

requestFields.name: termDuration
requestFields.note: ISO 8601; defaults to the legacy value

requestFields.name: addOnMigrations
requestFields.note: FLAT list of add-ons, not nested

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/migrations/newcommerce`, { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ currentSubscriptionId }) });

gotchas: Only currentSubscriptionId is required; termDuration, billingCycle, purchaseFullTerm, quantity, customTermEndDate are optional and let you change terms during migration.
Omitted properties carry forward the legacy subscription's values.
Base subscriptions migrate together with all active add-ons as a bundle; if any add-on is ineligible the whole bundle fails.
addOnMigrations must be a FLAT list, not nested.
Call validate-migration first - it reports eligibility and the exact reasons this POST would otherwise fail with.
Migration is asynchronous: poll get-migration with the returned migration id, and use get-migration-events for the step-by-step trail.
To schedule rather than run immediately, use create-migration-schedule.

scenarios.title: Get a collection of invoices
gotchas: size/offset are only honored for legacy invoices; for modern commercial purchases they are ignored.
Use the filter param (LeftFilter/RightFilter/Operator JSON, bounded by InvoiceDate) to avoid timeouts on large invoice sets.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

scenarios.title: Get an invoice by ID
gotchas: invoice-id is a string identifier, not a GUID.
App+User only (no app-only).
For modern commercial purchases this applies only to daily-rated usage and recons generated before 2025-05-15.

scenarios.title: Get a customer's Azure utilization records

examples.csharp:
var url = $"/v1/customers/{customerId}/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/utilizations/azure?start_time={Uri.EscapeDataString(start)}&end_time={Uri.EscapeDataString(end)}&granularity=daily&show_details=true";
var res = await http.GetAsync(url);
examples.typescript:
const qs = new URLSearchParams({ start_time: start, end_time: end, granularity: "daily", show_details: "true" });
const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/subscriptions/${subscriptionId}/utilizations/azure?${qs}`, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });

gotchas: start_time and end_time are REQUIRED (UTC date-time offset). granularity (daily default), show_details (default true), and size (max 1000) are optional.
NOT supported for Azure plans (only legacy MS-AZR-0145P); for Azure plans use the invoice consumption line-item APIs.
If data isn't ready in billing yet, returns 204 with a Retry-After header.
Paged - follow the next link.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

scenarios.title: Get the partner's current account balance

examples.csharp: var res = await http.GetAsync("/v1/invoices/summary"); // read BalanceAmount

gotchas: The balance is exposed via InvoiceSummary.BalanceAmount; there is no dedicated balance endpoint.
Use /v1/invoices/summaries (plural) for one summary per currency.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

scenarios.title: Validate an address

requestFields.name: country
requestFields.note: ISO alpha-2 code

requestFields.name: postalCode
requestFields.note: required in most countries

requestFields.name: state
requestFields.note: required in some countries

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch("https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/validations/address", { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body });

gotchas: Prevalidate addresses before create-customer or profile updates; the caller picks the final address from the result.
Country must be the two-character ISO alpha-2 code; required fields vary by country/region.
Only Verified or VerifiedShippable are safe to use directly; other statuses need user confirmation.

scenarios.title: Verify domain availability

examples.typescript:
const res = await fetch("https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/domains/contoso.onmicrosoft.com", { method: "HEAD", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
const available = res.status === 404;

gotchas: Use the HEAD method - there is no response body; rely on the status code.
404 Not Found means the domain IS available; 200 OK means it is already in use.
The {domain} segment is the full domain string, e.g. contoso.onmicrosoft.com.

scenarios.title: Get a record of Partner Center activity
gotchas: Activity log data is limited to the previous 90 days; a startDate older than 90 days returns 400.
Without startDate, results default to the previous 30 days. Dates use yyyy-mm-dd.
filter must be url-encoded JSON with Field/Value/Operator (fields: CompanyName substring, CustomerId equals, ResourceType equals); matching is case-insensitive.
Results are paged.

scenarios.title: Get all service requests for a customer
gotchas: App+User only (no app-only).
For a single service request use GET /v1/servicerequests/{servicerequest-id}; that endpoint accepts an IncludeOrganizationRequests header for the Support Request Admin role.

scenarios.title: Get per-request MFA compliance for App+User API calls
gotchas: App+User only. Returns the most recent App+User API requests, capped at 10K items.
Each item exposes mfaCompliant (true/false) plus upn, objectId, applicationId, operationName - use it to find non-MFA-compliant callers before the MFA enforcement date.
This is request-level telemetry, not a static per-user enrollment record.

scenarios.title: Get customer licenses usage information
gotchas: App+User only. Returns CustomerLicensesUsageInsights (workloadName, productName, licensesActive, licensesQualified, usagePercent).
Superseded by the workload-level GET /v1/analytics/commercial/usage/license/, but this per-customer endpoint remains documented and valid.

scenarios.title: Create a New Commerce transfer (billing ownership)

headers.name: Authorization
headers.note: Bearer token, audience https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com; caller must be an Admin agent

requestFields.name: sourcePartnerTenantId
requestFields.note: the source/current partner tenant

requestFields.name: customerEmailId
requestFields.note: receives transfer notifications

requestFields.name: transferType
requestFields.note: 3 = NewCommerce (Azure plan + NCE license-based)

requestFields.name: targetProductTypes
requestFields.note: AzureSubscription, AzureReservation, AzureSavingsPlan, OnlineServicesNCE; null = all

requestFields.name: partnerOnRecord
requestFields.note: MPN ID; only when target is an indirect provider

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/transfers`, { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body });

gotchas: The TARGET (new) partner creates the transfer; the SOURCE partner later submits it. Only Admin agents can create transfers.
transferType must be 3 (NewCommerce) - this endpoint is not for legacy subscriptions.
Customer must already have a reseller relationship with the target partner.
Returns 201 with status Pending. Common errors: 900400, 900160, 20002.

scenarios.title: Get a transfer by ID
gotchas: Either the source or target partner can read transfer status (Pending -> InProgress -> Complete).
Target partners cannot see line items until the transfer completes (new subscription/order IDs are issued then).

scenarios.title: Get a customer's Azure reservations (entitlements)
gotchas: Partner Center has no 'reservation orders' endpoint; reservations are 'reservedinstance' entitlements, each carrying a referenceOrder.id and entitledArtifacts links.
Omit entitlementType to return all entitlement types; add showExpiry=true for expiry dates.
Reservation orders have billingCycle one_time; fetch the order itself via get-order-by-id with referenceOrder.id.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

scenarios.title: Get customer agreements (MCA confirmation)
gotchas: App+User only (no app-only).
If agreementType is omitted it defaults to MicrosoftCloudAgreement; pass MicrosoftCustomerAgreement explicitly for MCA confirmations.
Agreement resource is supported only in the Microsoft public cloud (not 21Vianet or US Gov).
Returns a paged collection.

scenarios.title: Get the Azure rate card (real-time prices)

headers.name: X-Locale
headers.note: e.g. en-US; also drives region/currency defaults

gotchas: currency (ISO, default USD) and region (ISO country, default US) are optional; prices vary by market.
Response can be very large (~1.5 MB) - stream/parse efficiently.
All rates are pretax (isTaxIncluded is always false).
Use /v1/ratecards/azure-shared for Azure Partner Shared Services pricing.

scenarios.title: List GDAP delegated admin relationships (Microsoft Graph)

headers.name: Authorization
headers.note: Bearer token, audience https://graph.microsoft.com (NOT partnercenter); scope DelegatedAdminRelationship.Read.All

gotchas: This is a Microsoft Graph API, NOT Partner Center: host graph.microsoft.com, path starts with /v1.0/. A Partner Center token will not work.
Needs a Graph token with scope DelegatedAdminRelationship.Read.All (or ReadWrite.All); caller is in the partner tenant.
Supports OData $select/$filter/$top (max 300)/$orderby; paged via @odata.nextLink.
Not available in China (21Vianet); available in Global and US Gov.

scenarios.title: Get eligible subscription transitions (NCE)
gotchas: eligibilityType is optional (default immediate); use the returned catalogItemId as toCatalogItemId in create-subscription-transition.
Distinct from GET .../transitions, which returns transition history rather than eligible transitions.
Empty list for trials or when eligibilityType=scheduled (you can only transition into an existing subscription via an immediate transition).

scenarios.title: Create a subscription transition (NCE upgrade / trial-to-paid)

requestFields.name: toCatalogItemId
requestFields.note: target product:sku:availability from transitionEligibilities

requestFields.name: quantity
requestFields.note: number of licenses to transition

requestFields.name: transitionType
requestFields.note: transition_only or transition_with_license_transfer

requestFields.name: toSubscriptionId
requestFields.note: transition into an existing subscription (immediate only)

requestFields.name: termDuration
requestFields.note: ISO 8601, e.g. P1M / P1Y

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/subscriptions/${subscriptionId}/transitions`, { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body });

gotchas: Two-step: GET transitionEligibilities first to get a valid toCatalogItemId, then POST.
Used to upgrade an NCE subscription to a target SKU/term and to convert an NCE trial to paid.
transition_with_license_transfer needs Directory Writer (GDAP); provisioning is asynchronous (response has an Events array).

scenarios.title: Upgrade a customer to the Azure plan

requestFields.name: customerId
requestFields.note: the customer tenant id

requestFields.name: productFamily
requestFields.note: "Azure" (upgrades legacy MS-AZR-0145P to the Azure plan)

examples.csharp: var res = await http.PostAsync("/v1/productupgrades", content); var location = res.Headers.Location; // productUpgrades/{id}
examples.typescript: const res = await fetch("https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/productupgrades", { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body });

gotchas: Global /v1/productupgrades collection (not subscription-scoped); the customer is identified in the body.
Returns 202 Accepted with an empty body and a Location header (productUpgrades/{id}) to poll; app+user only.
Check eligibility first via POST /v1/productUpgrades/eligibility. After upgrade, Get Subscriptions returns only the Azure plan.

scenarios.title: Get invoice billed reconciliation line items

headers.name: MS-ContinuationToken
headers.note: from the previous response's links.next when seekOperation=Next

gotchas: billing-provider: OneTime (modern), or Azure/Office (legacy). invoice-line-item-type: BillingLineItems or UsageLineItems.
OneTime pages via seekOperation=Next + the MS-ContinuationToken header (from links.next); Azure/Office use size+offset. Default/max size 2000.
This v1 API is in feature freeze; for new-commerce billed recon after 2025-04-21 use the async Graph v2 API.

scenarios.title: Get unbilled reconciliation line items

headers.name: MS-ContinuationToken
headers.note: from the previous response's links.next when seekOperation=Next

gotchas: Literal path /invoices/unbilled/lineitems (no invoice-id). Required query: provider, invoicelineitemtype, currencycode, period (current|previous).
Pages via size (max 2000) + seekOperation=Next with MS-ContinuationToken; allow up to 24h for unbilled data.
This v1 NCE API is deprecated effective 2026-03-15; use the async v2 GA unbilled API.

scenarios.title: Download an invoice statement (PDF)

examples.typescript:
const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/invoices/${invoiceId}/documents/statement`, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });
const pdf = Buffer.from(await res.arrayBuffer());

gotchas: App+User only. Response is a binary PDF (Content-Type application/pdf) - read it as bytes, not JSON.
Path is /documents/statement (singular). For Taiwan tax receipts use .../receipts/{receipt-id}/documents/statement.

scenarios.title: Get available offer promotions
gotchas: country and segment are required; segment currently supports only 'commercial'.
Returns only currently-active promotions (by start/end dates). Covers NCE license-based promotions.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

scenarios.title: Get a promotion by ID
gotchas: country is required; promotion-id is a delimited product:sku:availability string - URL-encode it.
Returns the promotion ignoring start/end dates (works after expiry - useful for reconciliation).
Response may include promotionConstraints for eligibility checks. Supports both app-only and app+user.

scenarios.title: Get a product by ID
gotchas: country is required; 404 with error 400013 if not found.
A product is a grouping construct and is not itself purchasable - drill into SKUs/availabilities.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

scenarios.title: Get a SKU by ID
gotchas: country is required; 404 with error 400013 (product) or 400018 (SKU) if not found.
If purchasePrerequisites contains 'InventoryCheck' you must call Check Inventory before ordering.
Supports both app-only and app+user.

scenarios.title: Confirm customer acceptance of the MCA (create agreement)

requestFields.name: primaryContact
requestFields.note: who accepted: firstName, lastName, email (phoneNumber optional)

requestFields.name: dateAgreed
requestFields.note: UTC date-time of acceptance

requestFields.name: templateId
requestFields.note: from Get agreement metadata for the MCA

requestFields.name: type
requestFields.note: "MicrosoftCustomerAgreement"

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/agreements`, { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body });

gotchas: App+User only; public cloud only (not 21Vianet or US Gov). Get the templateId via Get agreement metadata first.
201 Created on success; userId is derived from the App+User token.
Re-creating with identical contact fields returns error 600061 - vary at least one field to create another.

scenarios.title: Get a download link for the MCA template
gotchas: App+User only; public cloud + MCA only. Top-level /v1/agreementtemplates path (not under /customers).
country/language default to US/en-US; values are case-sensitive.
downloadUri (Word) and displayUri (preview) are freshly generated and EXPIRE after five minutes.

scenarios.title: Get a customer's qualifications
gotchas: Supports both app-only and app+user (unlike update-customer-qualification, which is app+user only).
Returns an array; a customer can hold multiple (e.g. Education + StateOwnedEntity).
Values: Education, GovernmentCommunityCloud, StateOwnedEntity, Nonprofit, None; vetted types carry vettingStatus.

scenarios.title: Set a customer's qualification

requestFields.name: qualification
requestFields.note: settable: Education, GovernmentCommunityCloud, StateOwnedEntity (None/Nonprofit cannot be set)

requestFields.name: educationSegment
requestFields.note: required when Education: K12 or HigherEducation

requestFields.name: validationCode
requestFields.note: required when GovernmentCommunityCloud

requestFields.name: website
requestFields.note: optional, for Education

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/qualifications`, { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body });

gotchas: POST (not PUT); app+user only. Only Education, GovernmentCommunityCloud, StateOwnedEntity can be set.
Education requires educationSegment (K12 or HigherEducation); GCC requires a validationCode + a GDAP role.
Vetted types (Education/GCC) start in a review/vetting flow rather than immediately Approved.

scenarios.title: Check inventory for catalog items before ordering

requestFields.name: TargetItems
requestFields.note: each needs ProductId; SkuId optional

requestFields.name: InventoryContext

Accepting is what actually moves billing ownership; poll get-transfer until the status leaves InProgress.
To decline instead use reject-transfer (a PATCH with status "reject").

Same URI as update-transfer - what differs is the status value in the body.
Rejecting leaves the subscriptions with the current partner unchanged.

requestFields.name: id

var req = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Patch, $"/v1/customers/{customerId}/transfers/{transferId}") { Content = content };

Same URI as reject-transfer; "Cancel" is the creating partner backing out, "reject" is the source partner declining.
Once a transfer completes it cannot be undone here - the subscriptions have to be transferred back.

scenarios.title: Withdraw a transfer

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/transfers/${transferId}`, { method: "DELETE", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });

gotchas: The only DELETE in the transfer lifecycle; accept is a POST and reject/cancel are PATCHes on the same resource.
Only the partner that created the transfer can withdraw it, and only while it is still pending.

scenarios.title: Rename a subscription (nickname)

requestFields.name: (full Subscription resource)
requestFields.note: GET the subscription, mutate, then PATCH the whole object back

gotchas: The API field is friendlyName; "nickname" is only what the Partner Center UI calls it.
Cosmetic, but still a full-resource PATCH: include autoRenewEnabled or it resets to false.
The name is partner-facing disambiguation only - it does not change what the customer is billed for.

scenarios.title: Get a subscription's support contact
gotchas: Support contact is per SUBSCRIPTION, not per customer - two subscriptions of one customer can be supported by different partners.
In indirect (two-tier) CSP this is how you tell whether the reseller or the provider owns support for a subscription.

scenarios.title: Set a subscription's support contact

requestFields.name: supportTenantId
requestFields.note: tenant of the partner taking over support

requestFields.name: supportMpnId
requestFields.note: that partner's MPN id

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/subscriptions/${subscriptionId}/supportcontact`, { method: "PUT", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body });

gotchas: PUT, not PATCH - the body replaces the whole support contact.
The target partner must already have a relationship with the customer, otherwise the call is rejected.
Set per subscription, so moving support for a customer means iterating their subscriptions.

scenarios.title: Search customers by company name or domain

examples.typescript:
const filter = encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify({ Field: "CompanyName", Value: "Cont", Operator: "starts_with" }));
const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers?size=0&filter=${filter}`, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });

gotchas: filter is a URL-ENCODED JSON object: {"Field":"CompanyName","Value":"Cont","Operator":"starts_with"}. Sending it unencoded is the usual 400.
starts_with is the only operator this endpoint supports - there is no contains or equals.
Field accepts CompanyName or Domain.
Same route as list-customers; that entry is the unfiltered listing.

scenarios.title: Get a customer's company profile
gotchas: Returns tenantId, companyName and the customer's primary domain - the domain is what you need when inviting users or checking a duplicate tenant.
get-customer-by-id returns the same profile nested; this route is for when you only want the company block.
The company profile is read-only through the API; the customer changes it in their own tenant.

scenarios.title: Get a customer's billing profile
gotchas: Read this before update-customer-billing-profile: the write is a PUT of the whole profile and needs the ETag this response carries.
Holds the billing email, culture, language and default address - the address that address validation rules (get-country-validation-rules) apply to.
This is the CUSTOMER's billing profile; the partner's own is get-billing-profile.

scenarios.title: Update a customer's billing profile

headers.name: If-Match
headers.note: the ETag from the GET; required for concurrency detection

requestFields.name: (full CustomerBillingProfile resource)
requestFields.note: PUT replaces the profile - GET it, mutate, send it all back

requestFields.name: email
requestFields.note: billing contact address

requestFields.name: culture
requestFields.note: e.g. en-US

requestFields.name: defaultAddress
requestFields.note: must satisfy the market's rules - see get-country-validation-rules

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/profiles/billing`, { method: "PUT", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json", "If-Match": etag }, body });

gotchas: If-Match with the ETag from the GET is REQUIRED; without it, or with a stale one, the write fails with 2055.
PUT, not PATCH: the body replaces the profile, so send every field you want to keep.
Validate the address against the market's rules first (get-country-validation-rules, validate-address) - a rejected address blocks transacting.

scenarios.title: Get a customer's organization profile
gotchas: Organization-level tenant detail, distinct from the company profile returned by get-customer-company-profile.
Useful when reconciling a customer the partner did not create, where the company profile alone is ambiguous.

scenarios.title: Get a customer's custom domains
gotchas: Lists the domains already added to the customer tenant - check here before creating users, because a user's UPN must use one of them.
The onmicrosoft.com default domain is on the company profile, not necessarily in this list.
To register another one use add-verified-domain; to check whether a domain is free use check-domain-availability.

scenarios.title: Add a verified domain to a customer

requestFields.name: verifiedDomainName
requestFields.note: the domain being added

requestFields.name: domain
requestFields.note: the domain information block

requestFields.name: domainFederationSettings
requestFields.note: federation configuration for the domain

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/verifieddomain`, { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body });

gotchas: This RECORDS a domain that is already verified; it does not perform DNS verification. Verify in the customer tenant first or the call is rejected.
Read the current list with get-customer-custom-domains before adding, to avoid a duplicate.
Adding a federated domain changes how the customer's users sign in - do not do it as a side effect of onboarding.

scenarios.title: Get a customer's account validation status
gotchas: App+User credentials only - an app-only token is rejected with 900329.
type=account is the documented validation type; the status is what decides whether the customer may transact at all.
A customer under review fails purchases with 800075 - check here before blaming the cart.

scenarios.title: Get the partner's Government Community Cloud validation codes
gotchas: US GOVERNMENT ONLY (Partner Center for Microsoft Cloud for US Government). A validation code is required to create a customer in the Government Community Cloud.
"all" is a literal path segment here, not a placeholder for a customer id.
Irrelevant in the commercial cloud - create-customer needs no validation code there.

scenarios.title: Get address formatting rules for a market
gotchas: The two-character ISO country code is the path segment - the market, not a language.
Tells you which address fields are required, whether a state/region list is fixed, and the postal-code format - drive your address form from this rather than hardcoding per country.
validate-address enforces these same rules; call this first if you want to fail in the UI rather than at the API.

scenarios.title: Get a customer user account by ID
gotchas: Read the user before any PATCH: user writes replace the object, so you need the current values.
Returns the user's state, which is how you tell an active account from a soft-deleted one (see list-deleted-users).
Licences assigned to the user are a separate call - get-user-licenses.

scenarios.title: Get the directory roles assigned to a customer user
gotchas: The same page documents two sibling routes: GET .../directoryroles lists every role in the customer tenant, and GET .../directoryroles/{role-id}/usermembers lists the members of one role. This entry is the per-user view.
Read this before offboarding - remove-user-role needs the role ids, and deleting a user who still holds a privileged role leaves the role unattended.
Roles here are Microsoft Entra directory roles in the CUSTOMER tenant, not Partner Center roles and not GDAP roles.

scenarios.title: Update a customer user account

requestFields.name: (full CustomerUser resource)
requestFields.note: GET the user, mutate, then PATCH the whole object back

requestFields.name: userPrincipalName
requestFields.note: must use a domain registered on the customer tenant - see get-customer-custom-domains

examples.csharp:
var req = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Patch, $"/v1/customers/{customerId}/users") { Content = content };
var res = await http.SendAsync(req);
examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/users`, { method: "PATCH", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body });

gotchas: The route is the COLLECTION (/users) with no user id in the path - the user being updated is identified by the id inside the body. This is easy to get wrong because reset-password and delete-user both take /users/{user-id}.
App+User credentials only.
Changing userPrincipalName changes how the user signs in; the new domain must already be on the tenant.

scenarios.title: List a customer's deleted users

examples.typescript:
const filter = encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify({ Field: "UserState", Value: "Inactive", Operator: "equals" }));
const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/users?size=0&filter=${filter}`, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });

gotchas: There is no separate deleted-users endpoint: it is the user list with a URL-ENCODED filter {"Field":"UserState","Value":"Inactive","Operator":"equals"}.
A deleted account stays recoverable for 30 days - restore-user brings it back within that window, after which it is gone.
Its licences are released on deletion, so restoring a user does not restore their licences; reassign with assign-licenses.

scenarios.title: Remove the reseller relationship with a customer

requestFields.name: relationshipToPartner
requestFields.note: set to "none" to end the reseller relationship

examples.csharp:
var req = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Patch, $"/v1/customers/{customerId}") { Content = content };
var res = await http.SendAsync(req);
examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}`, { method: "PATCH", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ relationshipToPartner: "none" }) });

gotchas: Ends BILLING ownership. Distinct from remove-delegated-admin, which uses the same URI and method but sets allowDelegatedAccess false and only drops admin access - read the field, not the route, to know which one you are sending.
Irreversible from the partner side: re-establishing it needs the customer to accept a fresh invitation (get-reseller-relationship-url).
Active subscriptions do not disappear; they stop being this partner's to bill and manage, so settle transfers first.

scenarios.title: Remove delegated admin access to a customer

requestFields.name: allowDelegatedAccess
requestFields.note: set to false to drop delegated admin privileges

examples.csharp:
var req = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Patch, $"/v1/customers/{customerId}") { Content = content };
var res = await http.SendAsync(req);
examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}`, { method: "PATCH", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ allowDelegatedAccess: false }) });

gotchas: Drops ADMIN ACCESS only; billing ownership survives. Distinct from remove-reseller-relationship, which uses the same URI and method but sets relationshipToPartner to "none".
This is the legacy DAP switch. Granular access is governed by GDAP relationships - terminate those with delete-gdap-relationship or create-gdap-relationship-request.
Losing admin access breaks user and licence management for that customer; the subscriptions keep running.

scenarios.title: Create a customer for an indirect reseller

requestFields.name: billingProfile
requestFields.note: email, culture, language and default address

requestFields.name: companyProfile
requestFields.note: companyName and domain

requestFields.name: associatedPartnerId
requestFields.note: the indirect reseller this customer belongs to

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch("https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers", { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body });

gotchas: Same route as create-customer; associatedPartnerId is what makes it a two-tier (indirect provider on behalf of reseller) creation.
The indirect reseller must already be linked to the provider - list them with get-indirect-resellers.
The response carries userCredentials with the admin password exactly once. Save it; it is never returned again.

scenarios.title: List the customers of an indirect reseller

examples.typescript:
const filter = encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify({ Field: "IndirectReseller", Value: resellerId, Operator: "starts_with" }));
const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers?size=0&filter=${filter}`, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });

gotchas: URL-ENCODED filter with Field "IndirectReseller" and the reseller's tenant id as Value; the operator is starts_with.
Indirect provider view - it answers "which of my customers belong to this reseller".
Same route as list-customers and search-customers; only the filter differs.

scenarios.title: Get confirmation of a customer's agreement consent
gotchas: Unfiltered form of the route get-agreements filters with ?agreementType - use that one when you only care about a specific agreement.
An empty collection means no attested consent is on record, which blocks transacting for the customer.
This records the PARTNER's attestation. If the customer signed directly with Microsoft, that shows up in get-direct-sign-status instead.

scenarios.title: Get agreement metadata by agreement type
gotchas: Partner-wide metadata, not per customer: it returns the templateId and version you must quote when recording consent with create-agreement.
Quote the CURRENT templateId - recording consent against a superseded template is rejected.
See the agreementType enum for the accepted values.

scenarios.title: Check whether a customer signed the MCA directly with Microsoft
gotchas: Answers a different question from get-customer-consent: this is the customer signing the Microsoft Customer Agreement DIRECTLY with Microsoft, not the partner attesting on their behalf.
When it reports a direct signature, the partner does not need to collect and record an attestation with create-agreement.
Check it before onboarding an existing tenant - a direct signature is the usual explanation for an empty agreements collection on a customer who can nevertheless transact.

scenarios.title: Create a self-serve policy

headers.name: MS-RequestId
headers.note: GUID; the docs mark it required on this route

headers.name: MS-CorrelationId
headers.note: GUID; the docs mark it required on this route

requestFields.name: selfServeEntity
requestFields.note: who is granted access: selfServeEntityType (e.g. "customer") + tenantID

requestFields.name: grantor
requestFields.note: who grants it: grantorType (e.g. "billToPartner") + tenantID

requestFields.name: permissions
requestFields.note: the actions the entity may perform for itself

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch("https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/SelfServePolicy", { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body });

gotchas: Governs what the CUSTOMER may buy for themselves in the Microsoft admin center - it is a purchasing-permission policy, not a Partner Center role.
MS-RequestId and MS-CorrelationId are documented as required here, unlike most routes where they are merely advisable.
The route is capitalised SelfServePolicy; some hosts are case-sensitive about it.

scenarios.title: List self-serve policies for a customer
gotchas: entity_id is the CUSTOMER's tenant id - the entity access is requested for, not a policy id.
Required: without entity_id the request has no scope and is rejected.
Take the policy id from here for update-selfserve-policy and delete-selfserve-policy.

scenarios.title: Update a self-serve policy

headers.name: MS-RequestId
headers.note: GUID; the docs mark it required on this route

headers.name: MS-CorrelationId
headers.note: GUID; the docs mark it required on this route

requestFields.name: (full SelfServePolicy resource)
requestFields.note: PUT replaces the policy - GET it, mutate, send it all back

requestFields.name: permissions
requestFields.note: the full permission set that should remain in force

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/SelfServePolicy/${policyId}`, { method: "PUT", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body });

gotchas: PUT, not PATCH: omitting a permission removes it, so send the whole set.
policy-id comes from list-selfserve-policies, which is keyed by the customer's tenant id.
Removing a permission takes effect for the customer's own admin-center purchasing immediately.

scenarios.title: Delete a self-serve policy

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/SelfServePolicy/${policyId}`, { method: "DELETE", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });

gotchas: Removes the whole policy. To keep the policy but narrow it, PUT a smaller permission set with update-selfserve-policy instead.
After deletion the customer loses the self-serve purchasing the policy granted.
policy-id comes from list-selfserve-policies.

scenarios.title: Get a customer's managed services
gotchas: Returns the services the partner can administer for this customer, each with the deep link into that service's admin portal.
Requires delegated admin access - with DAP removed (remove-delegated-admin) or no GDAP relationship the list comes back empty.
An empty list on a customer with active subscriptions is an access problem, not a subscription problem.

scenarios.title: Update the partner's organization profile

requestFields.name: (full OrganizationProfile resource)
requestFields.note: PUT replaces the profile - GET it with get-organization-profile, mutate, send it all back

requestFields.name: address
requestFields.note: must satisfy the market's rules - see get-country-validation-rules

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch("https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/profiles/organization", { method: "PUT", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body });

gotchas: This is the PARTNER's own profile. A customer's equivalent is get-customer-organization - the routes look alike and the mistake is expensive.
PUT replaces the profile: read it with get-organization-profile first and send back everything you want to keep.
Validate the address against the market rules before sending; a rejected address leaves the profile unchanged.

scenarios.title: Create a device configuration policy (Autopilot)

requestFields.name: name
requestFields.note: friendly name of the policy

requestFields.name: category
requestFields.note: the policy category

requestFields.name: policySettings
requestFields.note: the settings applied to devices carrying this policy

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/policies`, { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body });

gotchas: Creating the policy does not apply it to anything - attach it to devices with update-device-policy.
Same route as get-configuration-policies, which lists the customer's policies.
policySettings is a flat array of setting names; an unknown setting is rejected for the whole policy.

scenarios.title: Get one device configuration policy
gotchas: Read it before update-configuration-policy, which is a PUT and replaces the whole policy.
policy-id comes from get-configuration-policies.
The response reports how many devices carry the policy - check it before deleting.

scenarios.title: Update a device configuration policy

requestFields.name: (full ConfigurationPolicy resource)
requestFields.note: PUT replaces the policy - GET it, mutate, send it all back

requestFields.name: policySettings
requestFields.note: the complete setting list that should remain in force

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/policies/${policyId}`, { method: "PUT", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body });

gotchas: PUT, not PATCH: a dropped policySettings entry is a removed setting.
The change reaches every device already carrying the policy - it is not scoped to new devices.
Devices that have already been provisioned keep their current configuration until they are reset.

scenarios.title: Delete a device configuration policy

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/policies/${policyId}`, { method: "DELETE", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });

gotchas: A policy still attached to devices cannot be deleted - detach them first with update-device-policy, then delete.
get-configuration-policy reports the device count, which is how you know whether it is detachable.
Deletion does not reconfigure devices already provisioned under the policy.

scenarios.title: List the devices in a device batch
gotchas: This is how you confirm an upload actually landed - get-device-batches only lists the batches, not their contents.
Each device carries the id needed by delete-device and update-device-policy.
Right after create-device-batch the list can be empty because the upload is asynchronous; poll get-device-batch-status first.

scenarios.title: Delete a device from a batch

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/deviceBatches/${deviceBatchId}/devices/${deviceId}`, { method: "DELETE", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } });

gotchas: Removes the device from the customer's Autopilot inventory; it does not wipe or unenroll a device already in service.
device-id comes from get-batch-devices, not from the hardware hash you uploaded.
A device already provisioned under a policy keeps that configuration after deletion.

scenarios.title: Apply a configuration policy to devices

requestFields.name: devices
requestFields.note: the devices to update, each identified by its device id

requestFields.name: devices[].policies
requestFields.note: policy assignments; an empty list detaches the device from its policy

examples.csharp:
var req = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Patch, $"/v1/customers/{customerId}/DevicePolicyUpdates") { Content = content };
var res = await http.SendAsync(req);
examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/DevicePolicyUpdates`, { method: "PATCH", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body });

gotchas: The route is DevicePolicyUpdates on the customer - not the policy and not the device. Its capitalisation is part of the path.
This is the only way to attach or detach a policy, and detaching is the prerequisite for delete-configuration-policy.
Asynchronous like the batch upload: it returns a tracking id in the Location header, so poll get-device-batch-status.

scenarios.title: Get the status of a device batch upload
gotchas: batchtracking-id is returned in the LOCATION header of create-device-batch and update-device-policy - it is not the device batch id.
Device uploads are asynchronous: this is the only way to learn that one finished, and the only place a per-device failure reason appears.
Poll until the status is terminal before calling get-batch-devices, or the device list comes back short.

scenarios.title: Get the partner's Azure usage summary
gotchas: UNBILLED estimates for the current billing period. These figures do not reconcile to an invoice - use the invoice line-item endpoints for anything you bill on.
Widest aggregation in this family: the whole partner. Narrow with get-customer-usage-summary or get-subscription-usage-summary.
App+User credentials only.

scenarios.title: Get Azure usage records for every customer
gotchas: UNBILLED estimates for the current period, one record per customer. Not a billing source.
The path has no {customer-id}: "customers" is literal and the endpoint spans every customer the partner has.
Daily rated usage generally appears about 24 hours after consumption, later depending on when meters report.

scenarios.title: Get one customer's Azure usage summary
gotchas: UNBILLED usage for the CURRENT billing period only; it is an estimate and will not match the invoice.
Daily rated unbilled usage is generally available about 24 hours after the fact, and later if the meters report late.

At the start of a month you may see nothing until the previous month's BILLED data has been delivered. That is expected, not a fault: once billed data lands, unbilled data from the start of the month appears.
App+User credentials only.

scenarios.title: Get Azure usage records for a customer's subscriptions
gotchas: UNBILLED estimates, broken down one record per subscription for this customer.
The route ends at the subscriptions COLLECTION with no subscription id - for one subscription use get-subscription-usage-summary.
Only Azure-consumption subscriptions report usage; seat-based subscriptions return nothing here.

scenarios.title: Get one subscription's Azure usage summary
gotchas: UNBILLED estimate for the current period on this subscription; the invoice is the billing truth.
A spending budget (get-usage-budget) is evaluated against figures like these, and it only notifies - it does not stop consumption.
For the breakdown behind the total use get-subscription-meter-usage or get-subscription-resource-usage.

scenarios.title: Get a subscription's usage broken down by meter
gotchas: UNBILLED estimates per METER - the billing dimension. get-subscription-resource-usage answers the same period per RESOURCE instead.
Meter-level detail is where an unexpected total is usually explained.
Figures lag consumption by roughly 24 hours.

scenarios.title: Get a subscription's usage broken down by resource
gotchas: UNBILLED estimates per RESOURCE, which is what you want when attributing spend back to a workload or a customer's team.
Its sibling get-subscription-meter-usage slices the same period by meter; the two totals agree, the breakdown does not.
Only Azure-consumption subscriptions report anything here.

scenarios.title: Get a subscription's monthly usage records by resource
gotchas: MONTHLY aggregation of UNBILLED usage per resource, as opposed to the current-period view of get-subscription-resource-usage.
Note the path shape: usagerecords/resources, not resourceusagerecords. Two different routes with nearly the same name.
Still an estimate - reconcile against the invoice line items before invoicing a customer.

scenarios.title: Get a customer's Azure spending budget
gotchas: The budget is a NOTIFICATION threshold. Azure keeps consuming past it; nothing is capped or stopped.
It is evaluated against unbilled usage estimates, which lag consumption by about 24 hours - a customer can pass the budget before anyone is told.
Read it before writing: update-usage-budget replaces the amount.

scenarios.title: Set a customer's Azure spending budget

requestFields.name: amount
requestFields.note: the new budget for the customer's Azure usage

examples.csharp:
var req = new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Patch, $"/v1/customers/{customerId}/usagebudget") { Content = content };
var res = await http.SendAsync(req);
examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/usagebudget`, { method: "PATCH", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ amount: 5000 }) });

gotchas: Setting a budget does not stop consumption. It is a notification threshold, not a hard cap, so do not sell it to a customer as spend protection.
To actually limit spend you have to act on the notification yourself - suspend the subscription or remove the Azure entitlement.
The budget applies to the customer's Azure usage as a whole, not per subscription.

scenarios.title: Get the overage setting for a customer's consumption subscriptions
gotchas: Overage decides where consumption beyond a prepaid commitment is billed. It is keyed by Azure entitlement, not by subscription id.
The route sits on the subscriptions COLLECTION and covers every consumption subscription the customer has.
Read it before update-subscription-overage, which is a PUT.

scenarios.title: Enable or disable overage for a consumption subscription

requestFields.name: azureEntitlementId
requestFields.note: the consumption subscription overage applies to

requestFields.name: overageEnabled
requestFields.note: whether overage is allowed for that entitlement

requestFields.name: partnerId
requestFields.note: the indirect reseller's PartnerID; two-tier (indirect provider) only

examples.typescript: const res = await fetch(`https://api.partnercenter.microsoft.com/v1/customers/${customerId}/subscriptions/overage`, { method: "PUT", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body });

gotchas: azureEntitlementId identifies the target, not a subscription id - get it from get-azure-entitlements.
partnerId only applies in the two-tier model, where an indirect provider sets overage on behalf of a reseller. Sending it in a direct-bill setup is wrong.
Disabling overage stops consumption beyond the commitment from being billable; it does not cap what Azure will run.

scenarios.title: Get a customer's service costs summary for a billing period
gotchas: This is the CUSTOMER-facing cost view for a closed billing period, not the partner invoice. The two answer different questions and can differ.
billing-period is an enum value, not a date - "MostRecent" is the usual one.
Unlike the usage endpoints these are settled figures, so they are the right basis for a customer-facing statement.

scenarios.title: Get a customer's service cost line items
gotchas: The per-line detail behind get-service-costs-summary, still customer-facing rather than the partner invoice.
Use these to build a customer statement; use the invoice line items (get-invoice-billed-lineitems) for what the partner actually owes Microsoft.
billing-period is the same enum used by the summary route.

scenarios.title: Get all invoice summaries for the partner
gotchas: Plural /summaries returns one summary per billing provider; the singular /v1/invoices/summary in get-partner-balance returns the account balance. Different routes, near-identical names.
Balances here are the partner's, not any one customer's.
For a specific invoice use get-invoice-by-id; this is the starting point when you do not know the invoice id yet.

scenarios.title: Get the estimate links for unbilled reconciliation
gotchas: Returns the links you follow to query unbilled reconciliation detail; it is a directory, not the data itself.
currencycode is required and scopes the estimate to one billing currency.
For new commerce prefer the async Graph v2 exports (get-unbilled-reconciliation-v2); see pc_whats_new for the v1 cutoff dates.

scenarios.title: Get billed commercial consumption line items
gotchas: invoicelineitemtype=usagelineitems returns metered CONSUMPTION. Its sibling invoicelineitemtype=billinglineitems (get-invoice-billed-lineitems) returns everything else on the same invoice - query both to reconcile a full invoice.
currencycode is required here, unlike the billinglineitems variant.
Large invoices page: add size and a 0-based offset, or use seekOperation to continue.

scenarios.title: Get unbilled commercial consumption line items
gotchas: The unbilled counterpart of get-invoice-billed-consumption, and the usagelineitems sibling of the billinglineitems route in get-invoice-unbilled-lineitems.
period selects current or previous; there is no invoice id because nothing has been invoiced yet.
Unbilled figures are estimates that can still move - do not invoice a customer from them.
Page large results with size and a 0-based offset.

scenarios.title: List a customer's orders by billing cycle type
gotchas: Same route as list-customer-orders; billingType narrows it to one billing cycle. See the billingCycle enum for the accepted values.
Useful when reconciling a monthly invoice against annual orders that do not appear on it.
The filter is on the ORDER's billing cycle, which can differ from the subscription's after a scheduled change.
